# The OCaml estate

OCaml is the primary host of the Effect model (ruling of 2026-09-04, `docs/research/
2026-09-04-ocaml-estate-and-parity.md`). This directory is one dune workspace that holds every
OCaml program of the estate. Its Lean half is the lake library `OCaml5` under `src/OCaml5/`
(root module `src/OCaml5.lean`). `STANDARDS.md` holds the estate to nine rules. Four govern form:

* libraries with thin drivers;
* one component per file, with a property list at its head;
* generated files marked and regenerable;
* a command behind every number in a report.

Five govern modeling: interfaces once and small, refusals as values, exact numbers and comparison
by type, mutation behind pure interfaces, and outside libraries by contract.

One runtime runs here: **the visible machine**, the Lean `RunMachine` itself. It runs in OCaml
as Lean's own compiler IR translated into typed OCaml (`gen/`). `engine/` is the host engine
under that generated machine (`docs/research/2026-09-08-engine-brief.md`). Every fiber, frame,
park token, pending resume and event is a field of one value. So a machine can be inspected,
serialised, moved between domains and messaged through the model's own decision alphabet.
The OCaml made from the machine's Lean definitions through LCNF stands for the machine
(decisions row 391). `eff/` is the Lean program IR `Eff` as an OCaml language, so OCaml can
author programs the Lean machine decodes exactly.

The routes that once stood beside it are on the local branch `archive/ocaml5-avatar` at
`14e6835`. The engine brief ruled one OCaml engine, `gen/`. The archive holds the avatar (the
same machine as OCaml 5 effect handlers, `avatar/`) and the daemon `effect4d` that served it
(`server/`). It holds the avatar's wasm host (`wasm/`), route 1's OCaml half (`link/`, whose host
core `engine/` re-homed) and the spike probes (`probes/`).

The Lean half, `src/OCaml5/`:

| module | what it is |
| --- | --- |
| `Ml/*` | the one OCaml syntax of the estate, cut to the forms its producers build: the LCNF backend, the `eff/` emitter, and the module language (`open`, module types, packed modules, private types) for the interop plan's P1 and P2 (`Syntax`); its generated fold (`Fold`, the derived group `MlFold`), and the canonical printer (`Render`) and the well-formedness checker (`Check`, which reads an `open` as the opened unit's scope), each an algebra of the fold |
| `Eff/*` | the `Eff` program IR as OCaml: the closed world read off the environment (`World`), the `eff/` library as modules of that syntax (`Emit`), the goldens and corpus (`Goldens`) |
| `Lcnf/*` | the LCNF → OCaml backend: dump, naming, the type rows as data (`TypeRows`), types, the translation rules, and the one primitive table (`Builtins`: one row for each Lean constant with its OCaml form, Lean's runtime column and its contract; the target's library with each evaluator's rule; the runtime library's functions a form names, with the definitions the target evaluator runs; the reserved names) |
| `Tools/*` | the `--run` drivers, each a thin `main` over a library module: `LcnfDump`/`LcnfGen` (the route and the engine), `EffGen` (over `Eff`), `EffWire` (the wire goldens), `CasGoldens` (the CAS goldens) |

`harness/truth/` (tracked beside this estate) is the Lean-vs-rc.112 exit differential over
the program corpus (`run-truth.ts`, bun, `Truth.lean`).

## Building

The switch is `opam switch effect4`: OCaml 5.1.1, dune 3.24, js_of_ocaml 5.7.1 pinned (the
modelled backend), the Jane Street v0.16 set. On the Mac every command runs through
`opam exec --switch=effect4`; on the PC the switch lives in WSL Ubuntu:

```bash
cd ocaml
opam exec --switch=effect4 -- dune build              # gen, eff, engine, clock
opam exec --switch=effect4 -- dune test eff gen clock
opam exec --switch=effect4 -- dune test engine        # reads the printed corpus through E4_LEAN_CORPUS
```

From the repository root, `make check-ocaml` re-cuts the LCNF group when the machine changed,
runs these three commands in `ocaml/`, then the engine's seam check
(`ocaml/engine/tools/gen-check.sh`). It depends on the printed corpus, the engine's fixtures and
the LCNF group, and `make check-full` names it (`Makefile`).

The Lean half is `lake build OCaml5` from the repository root.

## Generated, and how to regenerate

`docs/GENERATED.md` holds the inventory, the producers and the checks. `make gen` runs the
producers in dependency order. `make check-gen` refuses a committed file that differs from a
fresh run.

| generated | generator | command |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `eff/eff_types.ml`, `gen/api_gen.ml`, `engine/api_engine.ml`, `gen/closure-*.tsv` | `src/OCaml5/Tools/LcnfGen.lean` | `make gen-lcnf` (the recipe `gen/roots.json`; each file's header carries its command) |
| `engine/test/rocq/rocq_run.ml`, `engine/test/rocq/rocq_run.mli` | Rocq's extraction of `docs/research/2026-10-16-itrees/rocq/LaneExtract.v` (the opam switch `rocq`) | `bash docs/research/2026-10-16-itrees/reproduce.sh OUTDIR`: step 13 writes them and refuses a difference from the committed files below their header |
| `eff/eff_{ctors,wire,subterm,json,native,layout}.ml`, `eff/eff_manifest.txt`, `eff/goldens/*` | `src/OCaml5/Tools/EffGen.lean` | `lake env lean -M4096 --run src/OCaml5/Tools/EffGen.lean ocaml/eff` |
| `goldens/eff/*` | `src/OCaml5/Tools/EffWire.lean` | `lake env lean -M4096 --run src/OCaml5/Tools/EffWire.lean ocaml/goldens/eff` |
| `engine/cas/goldens/*` | `src/OCaml5/Tools/CasGoldens.lean` | `lake env lean -M4096 --run src/OCaml5/Tools/CasGoldens.lean ocaml/engine/cas/goldens` |

## Owed

* `engine/`: the carriers as Lean definitions over the six storage interfaces, made from LCNF.
  They retire the extern seam's rows, the prelude's bodies and the hand carriers. This is the
  lowering cleanup's LC-8 (`docs/research/2026-10-14-lowering-cleanup/prompt.md`);
* `gen/`: the session made from LCNF, with its byte entries (LC-7). It takes `api_gen.ml`'s place
  as the list oracle;
* `eff/`: the two theorems its report states (erase ⇒ `wellTyped`; encode/decode exactness).
